To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the features of the 2-dimensional Gaussian operator can be used to model human gaze patterns.
the image features that draw human fixations are similar to the derivatives of the Gaussian operator and that these features can be used to predict human fixations.
(1) human fixations are attracted by image features that resemble derivatives in the 2D Gaussians and (2) these features are not present in the general structure of the image.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: what are the image properties that draw the human gaze?
the question: What makes a region in an image visually salient?
the development of a data-driven approach for automatic fixation prediction and detection of saliency in an image.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach can be used to automatically detect regions of interest in an image, which are likely to attract human gaze.
the features extracted from eye-tracking data can be used to detect ‘visually important’ image regions.
the features extracted from human gaze patterns are similar to the ones that would be expected from random gaze.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
human fixations are drawn to regions in images that resemble the derivatives of a 2D Gaussian.
the features we extract at the point of human gaze are similar to the ones we extract from random fixations.
the image features that draw fixation are not the same as those that attract human gaze, but are similar to the image structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the human visual system is sensitive to low-level image features and that these features can be used as cues for predicting where humans will look in an image.
human gaze is attracted towards image structures similar to derivatives of the 1-D and 2-D Gaussian operators.
the visual saliency of an image can be described by the spatial distribution of a few image features.
